_comment: The authored world: what can be observed, and the thoughts that come of it. Empty on purpose -- the shore is being authored from scratch. `config/observations.placeholder.json` holds the old test content and is a reference for the authoring format (encounter shape, tiers, deeds, unlock_when clauses); it is NOT loaded. An encounter must author both halves -- something to observe AND something to do -- or it is dropped at load with a warning. Tunable -- edit + relaunch (dev reads assets from source).

roll._comment: Tuning for the thought roll + reward scaling. Coefficients only; the math lives in C++ (see include/Observations.h RollConfig).

_interact_reach_comment: World px from an encounter's box edge: get within this and it glows and can be observed. One knob for the whole game.

encounters._comment: PLACEHOLDER TEXT -- shape is final, words are a first draft to rewrite. One encounter = the whole person; tiers are what HE notices (his voice), deeds are his moves, result_text is HER voice (speaker). The chain demonstrated: observe her -> a thought lands -> the thought's id unlocks a deed -> her reply sets a flag -> a second thought builds on both.
encounters.speaker: mom

tiers.text: She is at the counter, already dressed. The kettle has been on a while.
She moves like the kitchen is a place she is holding still. Everything wiped twice.

add.label: Say good morning
add.result_text: Morning. There's toast, if you'll actually eat this time.

add._comment: Unlocked by NOTICING, not by menu-grinding: the thought below must land first.
add.label: Ask if she slept
add.result_text: I sleep fine. You're the one leaving with half a plan -- sit, eat something.

thoughts._comment: PLACEHOLDER TEXT. Perception: noticing her, from observing her. Its id becomes a memory that unlocks the ask.
thoughts.text: She was up before the kettle. The tired sits on her like it lives here.
thoughts.miss_text: Something about the way she stands. It slips away.

thoughts._comment: PLACEHOLDER TEXT. Reason: fusing the noticing with her deflection. emotional_weight carries it -- it opens nothing, it just matters.
thoughts.text: She answers questions about herself by feeding people. That is the whole answer.
thoughts.miss_text: Her answer wasn't an answer, but you can't say what it was instead.
